ai_technology: SCOPE DeepGCN structural-graph learning with ProtT5 sequence embeddings and a Gaussian auxiliary training objective

evidence.ai_role: Deep graph learning combined residue-level structure, evolutionary information and protein-language-model embeddings to rank candidate functional positions. These rankings guided new functional tests, linking the learned operation to measured enzyme activity rather than only benchmark performance.
evidence.tested: Model-prioritized positions were tested in four enzymes using activity assays with three independent experiments and reference-enzyme normalization. Eleven tested positions had 0–4.1% residual activity; protein expression was checked. Two tested copper-coordinating sites were explicitly already established, while other model-selected positions included active-pocket and distal contexts.
evidence.unknown: Activity loss does not prove that every position directly catalyzes a reaction; folding, stability or subunit organization can explain some effects. Selection of the tested sites using SCOPE makes relative-model comparisons descriptive, not unbiased. Known-site recovery is not counted as a new discovery, and independent replication or broad applicability remains unestablished.

organization: Northwest A&F University; Adelaide University; Monash University; Beijing University of Chemical Technology

source_review.scope: Primary 30-page preprint PDF relevant graph-model Methods, experimental enzyme selection, functional-test Results and Discussion caveats; primary bioRxiv version history. Supplementary tables not independently audited.

summary: A November 23, 2026 preprint used SCOPE, a learned structural-graph model, to prioritize enzyme positions for laboratory tests. Across four low-homology enzymes, substitutions at 11 selected positions left 0–4.1% of reference activity. The tested set included established sites and additional predicted positions, so the result is a bounded functional map rather than 11 newly discovered catalytic residues. Activity loss supports functional importance but can reflect stability or structural effects instead of direct reaction chemistry.
title: Graph-learning-guided tests identify functionally important enzyme positions
